Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going around the edge to (4,5), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,5). So my guess (around the edge to (3,1) from number 2) was wrong. Next I'll try down.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes around the edge to (4,1).
Going up, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,3). So the line goes down.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
The line must go right: around the edge to (1,2) is number 6, which comes later; up is number 8, which comes later.
Going up would force the line onto number 8 before its turn; going around the edge to (1,3) would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
The line must go right: around the edge to (1,4) is number 10, which comes later; up is number 11, which comes later.
Going right would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Going down would leave both cell (3,1) and number 8 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going right would strand number 8: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would wall in number 11, the last number. So the line goes up.
Cell (1,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
